assessments.reasoning: The hash-matched NIST archive scan shows the NBS title and January 1976 issue date on PDF page 3. The foreword on page 5 identifies MUMPS as a programming language and describes Part I MDC/28 as the MUMPS Development Committee's adopted narrative specification. PDF page 15 §1.1 identifies that language as its subject.

challenge.method: Compare the publication date and editorial role on the title and foreword with Part I and the 1976 NBS standards survey, including the committee and ANSI chronology. Check for conflation of dates, document authorities, and later aliases.
challenge.results: NBS publication in January 1976 is distinct from committee adoption of Part I on March 12, 1975. The later NBS survey lists the ANSI action as a separate process. The cited handbook supplies the MUMPS programming-language identity.

limitations: Active is the index classification. Later ANSI editions and naming aliases require their own applicable evidence.
